items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: I got a picture out there, Lips Page, Lips Page, Count Basie, myself, Dan Miner and Bing Page and Susan.

ctx.x: Always kept him way up in the sixes and hard notes, laying right next to that second alto. If you ever move away from that, the weight will go away from the section, because he didn't have a big heavy tone. Keep him up in there, and that's how that section sounded different. When he came out, they put in two regular tenors, Basie's section started sounding like Fletch Henderson or somebody else's section. Where the tone was concerned.
Right, yeah, because when you get -- yeah, when you get people later, like Buddy Tate and Don Bias, you've got a different thing going.

items.title: 52157_Count Basie oral history interview
items.q: "Then in 1935, I enlarged this band at the Reno Club in Kansas City and this eventually became my present organization -- Rushing, Page, Jog, Durham, Ed Lewis and Jack Washington."

ctx.x: All right. That's interesting. That's interesting. "There were some great musicians in that Moten band. Five of those musicians have played with me, right up to the present. In addition to Walter Page and Jimmy Rushing, there are Ed Lewis, my first trumpet player of long standing, Jack Washington, baritone sax and Jo Jones at the drums." We You also had such men as Eddie Durham, who played trombone. When did Eddie Durham start playing guitar?

items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: I named Basie the Count, so that's when they started to call him Count, from then on.

ctx.x: I mean, this is the same band that -- well, Buster Smith has taken Washington's place and Harlan Leonard is added for these records. But the band in 1929, you know, where they're doing -- I don't know whether you did any of those arrangements, see, right down there.

(Inaudible.) I did the Mary Lee, and Bootleg, I forgot now. Let's see, New Vine Street Blues I did, Bandbox. I didn't do the (inaudible), I don't think. Small Black I didn't do. (Inaudible) Blues, I might have did that. Yeah, I think so. Wished I Could Be Blue, I think I did that with Rushing. That To Do I did, Get Going I didn't do. I don't remember Lisa Lee. Would You Be My Baby, I think I did that. And the New Morton Swing, the Count -- I named Basie the Count, so that's when they started to call him Count,…
